items.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: when you’re playing with such wonderful players like Warren Vache and Harry Allen

ctx.x: How much time do you get — like you’re on a lot of the Arbors recordings now, and how much time do you typically get. This is a long question. But how many hours do those LPs — yeah LPs — do those CDs actually take, and do you know what’s coming before you get there?

Uh good question. Okay assuming I’m not the leader I have no clue what’s coming until I get there. So the session usually is booked for two four hour days, 12 to 4 on a Monday, 12 to 4 on a Tuesday. They’re usually consecutive days. And so you turn up at 12 and you might get a bunch of tunes in your hand. You might get a tune for a song. You know what I mean? Like we’re doing this song, here’s the music. Do that song. Here’s the next © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

song. Here’s — either you know it or they’ll give you a chart you know what I mean? If they’ve got a specific arrangement they’ll always pull a chart. And so if I’m not the leader I have no clue what we’re doing. If I’m the leader and I think the musicians don’t need to know until they get there, you know what I mean, like when you’re playing with such wonderful players like Warren Vache and Harry Allen, they can read and play through anything.
